title: SAS Confirms October 1 Launch for Copenhagen-Mumbai Route After Mid-Air Turnaround
excerpt: Scandinavian Airlines secures all regulatory approvals for its return to India after 17 years, with five weekly Airbus A330 flights connecting Denmark to Mumbai.
body:
• SAS will launch Copenhagen-Mumbai service on October 1, 2026, operating five times a week with an Airbus A330
  • The route's original June 2 launch failed when the inaugural flight turned back over Azerbaijan due to missing Indian regulatory approval
  • SAS says all necessary approvals are now in place, with flights already available for sale
  • The route positions Copenhagen as a gateway for Indian travelers to Scandinavia, Europe, and North America

Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) has confirmed October 1 as the launch date for its Copenhagen-Mumbai route, ending months of uncertainty after the airline's June inaugural flight was forced to turn around mid-air because it lacked the required Indian regulatory approval.

A Fresh Start After a False One

The airline announced the new date in an operational update on August 14, confirming that all necessary regulatory clearances have been secured. The Copenhagen-Mumbai service will operate five times a week with an Airbus A330, a route SAS had originally planned as a year-round connection between Scandinavia and India.

The first Copenhagen-Mumbai flight is scheduled for October 2, with the first return service from Mumbai to Copenhagen departing on October 3, according to Live From A Lounge. Flights from October 1 onwards are already available for sale.

The restart follows one of the more unusual airline launch stories of the year. On June 2, SAS flight SK969 departed Copenhagen for what was supposed to be the airline's return to India after a 17-year absence. The Airbus A330 was several hours into its journey, already over Azerbaijan, when it was forced to turn back. The reason: a final regulatory approval from the Indian authorities had not been received as expected.

"SAS completed all necessary operational and regulatory preparations for the launch following several months of planning and coordination. Based on ongoing discussions with the relevant authorities, SAS had every expectation that the remaining formal approval would be finalised while the flight was en route."

— SAS, in a statement after the June turnaround

Route Details and Connectivity

SAS will operate Copenhagen-Mumbai flights on Tuesdays, Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, departing at 13:10 local time and arriving in Mumbai at 01:30 the following morning. Return flights from Mumbai operate on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays, departing at 06:00 and arriving in Copenhagen at 11:45.

The Airbus A330-300 fleet features 32 lie-flat business class seats in a 1-2-1 configuration, 56 premium economy seats, and 178 economy class seats.

"India is a key global market — both in terms of growing demand and economic importance. With this new route, SAS contributes to strengthening Copenhagen's role as a global hub while supporting increased connectivity between India and Northern Europe, as well as between India and North America," SAS President and CEO Anko van der Werff said when the route was first announced.

What It Means for Indian Travelers

For the Indian diaspora in Scandinavia and travelers from India, the route offers more than just a connection to Copenhagen. SAS, which left Star Alliance and joined SkyTeam in 2024, positions Copenhagen as a hub for onward travel to cities across Scandinavia, Europe, and North America, including New York, Boston, and Toronto.

The route will complement Air India's existing Delhi-Copenhagen service. With Mumbai currently unserved on the Copenhagen route, SAS has a first-mover advantage in connecting India's financial capital directly to Scandinavia. IndiGo has also expressed interest in serving Copenhagen, though no firm launch date has been announced.

What's Next

After the embarrassment of the June turnaround, SAS has taken a more cautious approach. The August 14 update makes clear that the airline is no longer waiting on outstanding approvals — it says the clearances are in place and the route is ready. Whether the October launch goes smoothly will be closely watched by Indian travelers and diaspora members who stand to benefit from the connection.
